headline: Network & Cloud Engineer | Routing & Switching | AWS | Linux
summary: Electronics and Communications Engineering graduate with networking depth (CCNA curriculum and Huawei HCIA-Datacom course) applied in the cloud: multi-AZ VPC design, private subnets behind NAT, default-deny security groups, a WireGuard VPN with per-team ranges and a Squid proxy. Designed a two-floor building network in Cisco Packet Tracer; familiar with OSPF, BGP and MPLS concepts.

bullets.text: Completed intensive hands-on training in Linux administration, networking, CI/CD, containerization, and cloud infrastructure, culminating in end-to-end DevOps projects (see Projects).
Applied DevOps best practices to production-tier projects, covering CI/CD, GitOps, containerization, and infrastructure automation.

bullets.label: Infrastructure & Access
bullets.text: Enterprise-style RHEL environment on EC2 (VPN gateway, control, identity, utility and per-team workstations) in private subnets behind a NAT gateway, built with modular Terraform; reachable only through a WireGuard VPN with per-team ranges, firewalld and default-deny security groups.

bullets.label: Identity & Team Policy
bullets.text: FreeIPA centralizes users, DNS, Kerberos, HBAC and sudo rules per team; the utility server runs a Squid proxy with per-team internet rules, NFS home directories, centralized logging and backups.

bullets.label: Automation & Operations
bullets.text: Idempotent Ansible roles (EC2 dynamic inventory) handle SSH hardening, SELinux, firewalld, chrony and fleet patching; Bash scripts rebuild and test the lab, with tickets, runbooks and incident reports documenting changes.

bullets.label: Platform & Security
bullets.text: Five Python/FastAPI banking microservices and an NGINX frontend on EKS, built for financial correctness (fencing tokens, row-lock ordering). Versioned Terraform modules deploy through GitHub Actions (OIDC) and ArgoCD App-of-Apps, secured with default-deny NetworkPolicies, Istio mTLS, Gateway API and External Secrets Operator (IRSA).
Provisioned the VPC, EKS and RDS MySQL from versioned Terraform modules, with environment definitions on Terraform 1.10+ native S3 state locking.
Designed the network for a two-floor building in Cisco Packet Tracer using routers, switches and end devices.

Modular Terraform for a 3-tier AWS app (VPC, ALBs, Auto Scaling groups, RDS) with tier-isolated security groups, deployed through a Jenkins pipeline with a manual approval gate and monitored by CloudWatch alarms.
Three-tier app on Kubernetes secured with RBAC, default-deny NetworkPolicies, and Cilium FQDN-based egress rules, with Ingress and autoscaling.

paragraphs: I am applying for the Network Back Office Engineer role at Orbitel Networks. I combine network fundamentals from my engineering degree with hands-on cloud network design, and I would like to bring that to your network operations team.

Your posting asks for routing and switching with OSPF and BGP, and MPLS basics. My foundation is the CCNA curriculum and the Huawei HCIA-Datacom course, and I designed a two-floor building network in Cisco Packet Tracer with routers and switches. I am familiar with OSPF, BGP and MPLS concepts, though I have not run them on live carrier equipment, and I would rather say so plainly. On the practical side, I built a Linux lab on AWS where hosts sit in private subnets behind a NAT gateway with default-deny security groups, reachable only through a WireGuard VPN with per-team ranges, plus a Squid proxy with per-team rules. I documented every change with tickets, runbooks and incident reports.

My degree and networking courses gave me the fundamentals; building VPNs, proxies and segmented VPCs on AWS showed me how much of reliability and security is decided in the network. A back office role is where that discipline of careful, documented change matters every day. I would welcome a conversation about the role, and my CV is attached.

email_body:
I am applying for the Network Back Office Engineer role at Orbitel Networks.
My CV and cover letter are attached.
I bring networking fundamentals (CCNA curriculum, Huawei HCIA-Datacom course) and hands-on VPN, NAT and VPC work on AWS.
I would be glad to discuss the role.
why_this_role: It builds on the networks I have already built: a Cisco Packet Tracer building design, and a WireGuard VPN, NAT-fronted private subnets and a Squid proxy with per-team rules on AWS.
